plot: The night after the film contest, Big Bertha has a cold and must be well by sunrise to drive thirty kids to the farm; she asks only for one quiet night, but 'Team Get-Well' (Turbo's fast soup, Grumpy's dusty 1980 blanket, Hal's loud lullaby, Pip's seat-bouncing, headlight checks) keeps waking her and she gets worse; Bolt's notebook shows every sneeze comes right after a visit, so the helpers were the cause; they take the blanket away and park outside as silent guards, fall asleep themselves, and Bertha wakes well and drives the kids on time; lesson: sometimes the kindest help is doing just what they ask; then a letter invites Turbo to the City Race Team.

script.title: Shh! Bertha Needs ONE Quiet Night

set.place: Bertha's bus depot on Gear Street, a cold windy night until sunrise before the school farm trip

script.description: Team Get-Well tries very hard to help a sick Bertha. Maybe too hard. Inspector Bolt #23

beats.say: Ah... ah... ACHOO! Oh no. Not tonight. Not tonight!
Bertha! The farm trip is at sunrise! Thirty kids!
I know, love. I must get well by morning.
It was the night after the film contest. Cold and windy.
Big Bertha parked in her bus depot, sniffing and sneezing.
All I need is one quiet night. Just sleep. That's all.
Then sleep you shall. Good night, Bertha. Sweet dreams.
Bertha closed her eyes. The depot was quiet. For one minute.
Psst! Team! We can't just leave her alone! She needs help!
A get-well team! I'll be the boss of pillows!
And I'll be the boss of soup! Hot, fast soup!
I have a blanket. In my tow yard. Since nineteen eighty.
And I'll sing her a lullaby. I'm very good. Very loud.
Friends. She asked for one quiet night.
Quiet help! The quietest help in the world! Go, team!
At nine o'clock, Turbo zoomed in with a pot of soup.
Bertha! Wake up! Soup time! Careful, it's very fast soup!
Hmm? Oh. Thank you, love. Ah... ACHOO!
Bolt took out his little notebook. Nine o'clock. One sneeze.
At ten past nine, Grumpy brought his old blanket. Very dusty.
Here. Warm. A bit dusty. Dust is also warm.
ACHOO! ACHOO! Oh my. Thank you, Grumpy.
Bolt wrote again. Ten past nine. Two sneezes.
At twenty past nine, Hal began his lullaby.
Sleep, little bus, sleep! Sleep, sleep, SLEEEEP!
Hal, dear... that isn't very quiet... ACHOO!
She's getting worse! Not better! What do we do?
Only nine hours until sunrise! We need MORE help!
More help? Hmm. Or perhaps a different kind of help.
But nobody heard him. Team Get-Well was much too busy.
I'll fluff her pillows! Wait. Do buses have pillows?
Pip bounced on Bertha's seats to make them soft. Boing, boing!
Pip, darling... it's ten o'clock... I was nearly asleep.
Bolt wrote it down. Ten o'clock. Bouncing. One sneeze.
Eleven o'clock! Headlight check! Open your eyes, Bertha!
Turbo shone his bright headlights right into Bertha's eyes.
Too bright, love! ACHOO! ACHOO!
She's cold. More blanket. Blanket fixes everything.
Grumpy shook his dusty blanket. A big grey cloud went puff.
ACHOO! ACHOO! ACHOO!
She needs a stronger lullaby! I'll sing it twice as loud!
Hal, please. Midnight is not for loud singing.
Midnight came. Bertha's engine went cough, cough, rattle.
I'm so tired, my wipers are drooping.
Thirty kids are waiting for the farm. Will she make it?
If Bertha can't drive, no farm trip! No cows! No piglets!
I could take the kids! I'm big!
You're a moving truck. You have no seats. Only boxes.
Ah. Kids in boxes. That's not a good idea, is it?
Then Bolt looked at his little notebook. And he looked again.
Nine o'clock, soup. Sneeze. Ten past nine, blanket. Sneeze.
Song, sneeze. Bouncing, sneeze. Headlights, sneeze. Dust, sneeze!
Every sneeze comes right after one of us visits!
Us? But we're helping! We're Team Get-Well!
Bertha told us what she needed. One quiet night.
And we gave her soup, songs, dust and headlights.
My blanket... was the dust? Since nineteen eighty?
We were so busy helping, we forgot to listen.
Oh no. Team Get-Well was Team Keep-Awake.
Then let us give her what she asked for. Silence.
Grumpy took his dusty blanket home. Very, very quietly.
Then everyone parked in a row outside the depot. Like quiet guards.
Psst. Is this quiet enough? Am I being quiet?
Turbo. Shh.
No soup. No songs. No headlights. Just the wind.
And one by one, the quiet guards fell asleep too.
When the sun came up, a big yellow bus was wide awake.
Good morning, Wheelburg! No sneezes! I feel brand new!
Huh? What? Is it morning? Did we oversleep?
You did, my darlings. But I slept best of all.
Thank you for the quiet. It was the best present.
Sometimes the kindest help is doing just what they ask.
Even when what they ask is... nothing at all!
And Bertha drove thirty happy kids to the farm. Right on time.
Turbo! A letter came for you this morning. A fancy one!
For me? City Race Team? They want me to race?
In the big city? But Turbo... you'd have to leave!
What do you think Bolt will find next time? We'll find out in the next episode!
